The Indo-Greeks were the first dynasty to issue gold coins in India [d1][d3][d6][d7]. Multiple sources confirm this, noting that gold coins were introduced around 270 BC, with ruler Antiochus II being among the first to introduce them for economic reasons [d2]. The Indo-Greeks were also notable for being the first rulers whose coins could be definitively attributed to specific kings, unlike earlier punch-marked coins [d1][d7]. While the Kushans later became famous for their extensive gold coinage, the initial introduction of gold coins in India is consistently credited to the Indo-Greeks, with gold coin numbers increasing under the Kushans [d1][d7].
